findings.title: Migration crashes when no matching embed category exists
findings.description:
The category query immediately indexes `[0]['id']`. If `embed_category` was never configured, or its value no longer matches a category, the query returns no rows and indexing raises before the uncategorized fallback runs. This prevents migration even for sites that never enabled embedding.

Read the first row safely and handle an absent result explicitly. Add migration coverage for missing and stale category settings.

findings.title: Existing URL-form hosts are migrated without normalization
findings.description:
The migration inserts legacy host values verbatim, bypassing the normalization in `EmbeddableHost`’s validation callback. Consequently, an existing entry such as `https://example.com/path` remains stored in that form, while `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares it against only `URI(...).host`, namely `example.com`.

These entries stop authorizing embeds and topic retrieval after upgrading. Normalize migrated values to the same representation used by runtime lookup, and test migration of bare domains, schemes, and paths.

findings.title: Legacy setting values are interpolated directly into SQL
findings.description:
The host value `h` is inserted into a quoted SQL literal without escaping or binding. A stored value containing an apostrophe can break the migration; crafted content can alter the SQL executed with migration privileges.

Use bound parameters or the connection’s quoting facilities rather than string interpolation. Cover quote-containing legacy values in migration tests.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid domains with longer top-level domains
findings.description:
The `[a-z]{2,5}` suffix restricts top-level domains to five letters. Valid domains such as `example.museum` and `example.technology` therefore cannot be added through the new administration interface.

Use hostname validation that supports valid modern top-level domains, with tests for longer and internationalized domain representations.

findings.title: New controller specs do not exercise the endpoints
findings.description:
This spec checks only class inheritance; `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` does the same. Neither exercises the newly introduced HTTP behavior.

Add behavioral tests for listing hosts, creating and updating category mappings, deleting hosts, invalid input, missing records, and unauthorized requests. These should verify response status, serialized payloads, and persisted state—not merely controller ancestry.
